prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-01-29. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 1.04 |
| Retained earnings       | 87,663M |
| Current liabilities     | 38,980M |
| Current assets          | 40,596M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 18,677M |
| Total liabilities       | 111,269M |
| Total assets            | 130,169M |
| EBIT / operating income | 2,359M |
| Revenue                 | 12,717M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-01-29, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The reported leverage (equity = 14.3 % of assets; liabilities/equity > 5.9\times) combined with a current ratio of only 1.04 places the firm well below investment-grade norms for liquidity and capitalization. Positive retained earnings and an 18.5 % operating margin provide some offset, but are insufficient to support an investment-grade rating on the given data alone.
DECISION: BB
(The rating is placed at the upper end of the BB band because the modest profitability and positive retained-earnings stock still imply some capacity to service debt under stable conditions.)
